analyst_view.overall: This is the Rhine derby. Köln are unbeaten at home this season, and René Wagner says he wants an 'eklig' (nasty) game in which Köln win every duel. Ragnar Ache is fit again, and Mikey Moore may start. Leverkusen lost narrowly at Marseille in the Europa League on Thursday and have conceded 16 goals in eight league games. Carles Martínez is without Diaby, Tella, Terrier and Ben Seghir, and is hoping to bring Christian Kofane back into the squad after a thigh injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Leverkusen's defence has been leaky, with 16 conceded in eight league games, but their attack is thin beyond Schick and Maza, and Köln have been the league's least efficient finishers. These factors roughly balance, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Leverkusen's possession game and Köln's direct, duel-heavy approach fit the model's fairly even split. Nothing in the news moves this.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, which already reflects a derby and referee Felix Zwayer. Wagner has openly asked for an uncomfortable game in which Köln win every duel, and a Leverkusen side under pressure after Thursday's defeat could lose its composure, so we lean a little higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. One Köln preview describes Leverkusen's defence as offering many open shots around the box, and Köln at home tend to shoot a lot without being clinical. Leverkusen remain a strong attacking side even with absences, so we expect slightly more shots than the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Köln should get more attempts against a shaky Leverkusen back line, but their poor finishing and Leverkusen's missing forwards point the other way. We stay close to the model.
